item.title: The Chinese Yoke: Russia’s Return to Vassalship
item.description: In the 13th century, Muscovy, the medieval antecedent to modern Russia, was a small outpost on the periphery of Kyivan Rus. It would not emerge as a regional power until the Mongol conquest, where it became crucial in extracting taxes for tribute and maintaining the overlordship of the Khans in the region. item.title: SkyFoundry and the Future of American Drone Production at Scale
item.description: China and Russia are churning out millions of drones while the United States has little capacity to build them at scale. Rep. Pat Harrigan of North Carolina introduced the SkyFoundry Act to change this, and it got rolled into the latest National Defense Authorization Act. item.title: Command Responsibility at Home: Governors, the Guard, and Domestic Readiness
item.description: Late last year, the Supreme Court blocked an attempted National Guard deployment into the Chicago area — but months earlier, far from the headlines, a federal memo was already reshaping what Guard “readiness” means at home. The Supreme Court’s order was procedural, not a final merit ruling. item.title: Beyond the Missile: A Cost-Per-Effect Blueprint for the Future Force
item.description: Should the United States buy more destroyers, or would the money be better spent developing bases, munitions, or software?
